subject: Org-Shielding: SSO & Service-Identity cutover plan for OncoHealth
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Romero <alex.romero@oncohealth.com>, oncohealth-it@oncohealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Mar 2023 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Org-Shielding: SSO & Service-Identity cutover plan for OncoHealth

Hi Alex / OncoHealth IT team,

Thanks again for the discovery call earlier — good alignment on goals. I wanted to capture a concise sequencing proposal so we can lock dependencies and owners. Attached: a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a service-account matrix that maps required Redwood runtime identities to OncoHealth roles.

High-level proposed phases:
1) Staging integration (SSO metadata exchange + SCIM dry-run) — test user provisioning and attribute mapping against a sandbox org.
2) Canary (limited SCIM sync + IP allowlist to staging/GW) — create service accounts, enable prefix caching, validate ephemeral tokener refresh.
3) Production cutover (SAML enforce, SCIM sync, IP gating to prod clusters) — scheduled low-traffic window and rollback plan.

Open items we need from your side to schedule dates:
- Team that will produce SAML metadata (entityID / ACS) and where to upload Redwood SP metadata.
- Authoritative list of outbound firewall egress IPs to allow (and whether they will be static or from cloud NAT pools).
- Which groups should be mapped via SCIM (e.g., admins, devs, auditors) and the primary username attribute to use.
- Any org policies that would block service-account creation (we flagged a potential org policy in our scan).

Next steps I propose:
- Ben to send the cutover checklist with explicit owner tasks (API keys, service account roles, firewall rules).
- OncoHealth to return SAML metadata and a provisional IP list by EOD Thu 3/23.
- Short kickoff call next week to pick a canary window.

Attachments: OncoHealth_MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.pdf, oncohealth_service-account-matrix.xlsx

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Romero <alex.romero@oncohealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: oncohealth-it@oncohealth.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Mar 2023 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Org-Shielding: SSO & Service-Identity cutover plan for OncoHealth

Thanks Jasmine — appreciate the clear phases. A couple of quick clarifications from security here: 

- SCIM: we will need to preserve our existing group attributes (department, role, location). Can you confirm Redwood will accept group-level custom attributes and not just "displayName" / "members"?
- IPs: our security team rotates NAT egress across three pooled ranges during maintenance windows. Are you able to accept a CIDR range (e.g., 34.72.0.0/14) with a maintenance notice instead of a single static IP?
- Service accounts: our policy requires that all vendor service accounts are created as "nonhuman" identities with limited lifetime tokens and are listed in our asset inventory. Can your matrix include token rotation cadence and whether Redwood creates service accounts on behalf of the customer or the customer must create them in their cloud project?

I've attached OncoHealth's mini-security questionnaire for SAML/SCIM integrations (we filled a few answers already). Also: procurement has asked for a short SOW/PO supporting SCIM provisioning — can you send us the minimal DocuSign SOW for signature?

Alex
Dir. IT Ops, OncoHealth
attachments: OncoHealth_Security_Questions.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Romero <alex.romero@oncohealth.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Mar 2023 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Org-Shielding: SSO & Service-Identity cutover plan for OncoHealth

Alex — short answers up front, then a pragmatic plan.

SCIM: Redwood SCIM supports group custom attributes in the mapping layer. We can map department/role/location as custom attributes and preserve groups; we'll provide a sample mapping file (JSON Schema) for your IdP team.

IPs: We can accept CIDR ranges with a 48h maintenance notice. For production, we prefer announced ranges (static) but we can support pooled ranges for canary/staging with a stricter monitoring policy.

Service accounts: Redwood recommends customers create the cloud service accounts (so they live in your asset inventory) and grant us a short-term key with least privilege. We also support an option where Redwood-managed service identities are created, but those are treated as vendor-owned and have additional contractual controls. Token rotation: we rotate ephemeral session tokens every 12 hours by default; long-lived keys are discouraged.

Proposed technical checklist (owners in parens):
- Exchange SAML metadata and upload Redwood SP (Jasmine)
- Provide SCIM sample users + group CSV for mapping (OncoHealth IT)
- Create least-privilege service account in OncoHealth project and add redwood-scim@redwood (OncoHealth IT)
- Add Redwood egress CIDR(s) to your firewall list (OncoHealth SecOps)
- Staging smoke tests: user create, group assign, deprovision (Redwood + OncoHealth)
- Canary sync: enable SCIM sync for one group (e.g., devs) and monitor for 48h (oncohealth-it@oncohealth.com)
- Cutover runbook and rollback checklist (Ben / Ops)

I'll attach the SCIM mapping example to the shared drive folder. If these owners look right, suggest we pick target canary week of Apr 3.

—Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
